title: Crispy Orecchiette with Spicy Sausage & Collard Ragù

ingredients.raw: 2 ounces grated Parmigiano Reggiano (about 1/2 cup), plus more for serving
ingredients.name: parmigiano reggiano

ingredients.raw: 1 pound sweet Italian sausage, casings removed
ingredients.name: sweet italian sausage

ingredients.raw: 6 tablespoons extra-virgin olive oil, plus more for drizzling
ingredients.name: olive oil

ingredients.raw: 3 to 4 tablespoons chopped jarred Calabrian chiles
ingredients.name: calabrian chiles

instructions.text: Prep: Bring a large pot of heavily salted water to a boil. Thinly slice the shallots. Strip the leaves off the collard greens and slice crosswise into 1-inch-wide strips; discard the stems.

Cook the pasta: Drop the orecchiette into the boiling water, stir, and cook until al dente according to the package directions. Scoop out a few cups of pasta water before draining (you'll need quite a bit to help cook down the greens). Drizzle the drained pasta lightly with olive oil so it doesn't clump.

Start the ragù: In a large Dutch oven, heat several tablespoons olive oil over medium-high heat. When very hot, add the sausage, breaking it into golf ball-size chunks. Cook undisturbed until well browned, 3 to 4 minutes; flip and brown the second side, 1 to 2 minutes; transfer to a plate (it will still be slightly undercooked — it finishes later). Reduce the heat to medium-low, add the shallots and a big pinch of salt, and cook, stirring often, until jammy and cooked down, 4 minutes. Stir in the tomato paste and Calabrian chiles (hold some back if spice-averse) and cook, stirring, until the tomato paste begins to stick to the pot, 4 to 5 minutes. Add the collard greens and a few big splashes of the reserved pasta water, stir well, cover, and cook until the greens are tender, 4 to 5 minutes, adding more pasta water if the pot gets dry. The ragù should be nice and saucy. Remove from heat and keep covered.

Crisp the pasta: In a large nonstick skillet, heat 2 tablespoons olive oil over medium-high heat. Add about half the cooked pasta and cook undisturbed until the bottom is golden brown and crisp at the edges, 3 to 4 minutes. Add to the pot of ragù and repeat with the remaining pasta.

Finish: Return the pot to medium heat. Add the sausage back in, breaking it into smaller pieces, along with a big splash of reserved pasta water and a few big handfuls of grated Parm. Cook, stirring vigorously, until a thick sauce coats the pasta, 30 seconds. Squeeze in the juice of 1 lemon and stir to combine. Divide among bowls, tear the burrata (if using) into small pieces over the top, drizzle with more olive oil, sprinkle with more Parm, and serve.
